question: I really love Cecilus-kun and Arakiya-chan, so I was really shocked by the story in Sasageru IF where the two of them had a child. I'd love to hear about the circumstances and episodes that led up to that, if there are any.
answer:
When I was writing Sasageru, those two just went ahead and got married on their own, so I don't really know either (laughs).

It was only when I decided I wanted to write about 400 years in the future that I started thinking about it for the first time. When I thought about what kind of people would still be around 400 years later... there'd be Arakiya, whose lifespan had effectively become endless because she'd practically merged with a spirit, and Madelyn, who's a dragon-human, and so on. I was also able to bring in the grown-up versions of the quasi-spirits accompanying Julius, something I'd originally thought would be nice to do somewhere someday.

When I started thinking, “What is Arakiya's motivation for still being around in the present day (400 years later)?” protecting Vollachia would naturally be one of them, especially because of her connection with Priscilla. But if Cecilus were to disappear, Arakiya's mental balance would probably become seriously unstable. So maybe Cecilus is taking responsibility before he dies. But unfortunately, Cecilus's way of taking responsibility would be the Vollachian way, and Rowan-san wasn't exactly a good father—so, after considering all those things, I think I had Arakiya have descendants so that she wouldn't lose her reason for living.

I imagine the proposal itself was probably very casual. Cecilus is the type who acts once he's made up his mind, so he might have said something like, “Anya always challenges me, but I think it's about time I got a prize if I beat you.” Arakiya would then challenge him by saying, “You won't beat me, so sure,” giving him her word. After their usual playful back-and-forth, Cecilus wins and says, “Then let's get married,” and that's probably how they got married.

And then Arakiya, having already said what she said, would be like, “Gnnnnngh...” — followed by marriage, followed by a child, followed by their descendants eventually going extinct... I think that's probably how it went.

The details of the individual episodes might be a little rough, but I think that's roughly the idea as it stands now!
